page: Amazon Web Services c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, with one thread per core. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside vector instruction support covering AVX-512 extensions such as VNNI and BF16.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 1994.0 and elevated metrics in text processing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.79 GB/sec. Small-model LLM text generation also reaches the upper quartile at 280.04 tokens per second. Multi-core performance aligns with expected mid-range compute profiles, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 10286.0 and stress-ng throughput of 18308.68. However, memory bandwidth on large uncached read blocks drops into the lower quartile at 38.63 GB/sec, and larger 7B parameter LLM generation falls to 7.9 tokens per second.

The instance does not include integrated local instance storage and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, while the network interface operates at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs provisioned. In terms of resource allocation and cost efficiency, the dedicated physical cores and DDR5 memory deliver predictable computational throughput without paying for excess memory overhead. The c7a.2xlarge is suited for CPU-bound tasks, continuous integration and build pipelines, batch processing, static web serving, and distributed microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 8 dedicated vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz. The configuration excludes local storage and discrete GPUs, utilizing a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark data highlights top-quartile single-core CPU throughput, text processing, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside mid-range multi-core performance and average Redis operation rates. Large uncached memory read bandwidth and larger model LLM inference represent performance bottlenecks due to memory constraints. Delivering cost-effective compute density through its balanced 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the c7a.2xlarge is well positioned for continuous integration pipelines, batch compute workloads, web serving, and CPU-intensive microservices.
